TS0U.what: Owns Singapore offices (OUE Bayfront, One Raffles Place), hotels (Hilton and Crowne Plaza Changi) and Mandarin Gallery retail.
TS0U.rev: Commercial (office and retail) roughly 60% of net property income, hospitality ~40%. Entirely Singapore after the Shanghai divestment.
TS0U.gm: REIT metrics: gearing around 40%, hotel income linked to RevPAR, office occupancy above 95%.
TS0U.mgmt: Managed by OUE Limited as sponsor, which is controlled by the Lippo-linked Riady family interests.
TS0U.comp: Suntec REIT, Keppel REIT and CDL Hospitality Trusts.
TS0U.moat: Prime Singapore locations - One Raffles Place and OUE Bayfront - with hotel exposure to Changi and Orchard tourism.
TS0U.ind: Singapore office is stable; hotel RevPAR has normalised after the 2023-24 events-driven peak.
TS0U.risk: Hotel income normalising lower while refinancing costs stay high.
TS0U.implied: A high yield and deep discount to book imply the market expects flat to falling distributions.
TS0U.debate: Bulls say pure Singapore assets at a large discount with a high yield. Bears note gearing, a small portfolio and sponsor-related concerns.
TS0U.disprove: Hotel RevPAR declining; office reversions turning negative; gearing above 41%; distribution cut.

8C8U.what: Owns purpose-built worker dormitories and student accommodation, spun out of Centurion Corporation into a REIT in 2025.
8C8U.rev: Singapore worker accommodation is the majority of income, with UK and Australian student accommodation the rest.
8C8U.gm: Very high net property income margins (above 75%) - dormitories are cheap to operate with high occupancy and regulated bed supply.
8C8U.mgmt: Managed by Centurion Corporation as sponsor, which retains a substantial stake.
8C8U.comp: Other dormitory operators in Singapore, and student accommodation providers in the UK and Australia.
8C8U.moat: Singapore purpose-built dormitory licences are tightly controlled and supply is regulated after the pandemic reforms - a genuine regulatory moat.
8C8U.ind: Singapore construction and marine sectors need migrant worker beds; supply is capped by government policy.
8C8U.risk: A construction slowdown reducing worker numbers, or policy changes on dormitory standards requiring capital spending.
8C8U.implied: The yield implies stable occupancy near 99% and continued rental growth from a constrained bed supply.
8C8U.debate: Bulls say regulated supply plus near-full occupancy makes this the most defensive niche in Singapore real estate. Bears note a short listing history and concentration in one asset class.
8C8U.disprove: Occupancy falling below 97%; bed rates declining; new dormitory supply approvals rising; construction demand slowing.

CC3.what: Sells mobile, broadband and pay TV services plus cybersecurity solutions in Singapore.
CC3.rev: Telecommunications (mobile, broadband, entertainment) is the majority; cybersecurity (Ensign and D Crypt) the rest and a differentiator versus peers.
CC3.gm: Service EBITDA margin in the 20s. Singapore telecom is a four-player market with persistent price competition.
CC3.mgmt: Nikhil Eapen is CEO. Temasek and Asia Mobile Holdings hold a controlling interest.
CC3.comp: Singtel, M1 and Simba in Singapore mobile and broadband.
CC3.moat: Spectrum and network infrastructure plus a customer base - but Singapore has four operators for six million people, which caps pricing power.
CC3.ind: Singapore mobile is saturated and price-competitive; cybersecurity is growing.
CC3.risk: Continued mobile price competition from Simba and M1 eroding average revenue per user while transformation costs remain.
CC3.implied: A mid-teens P/E with a high dividend yield implies flat earnings and a sustained payout.
CC3.debate: Bulls say a well-covered dividend with cybersecurity optionality. Bears point at structural price competition in a tiny, saturated market.
CC3.disprove: Mobile service revenue declining; cybersecurity growth slowing; dividend not covered by free cash flow; market share loss.

9A4U.what: Owns logistics and industrial properties across Singapore, Australia, Japan and South Korea after merging several ESR-linked trusts.
9A4U.rev: Singapore is the largest share, with Australia, Japan and Korea providing diversification. New Economy assets (logistics, data centres) are the strategic focus.
9A4U.gm: REIT metrics: net property income margin around 73%, gearing around 40%, occupancy in the mid 90s.
9A4U.mgmt: Managed by ESR Group as sponsor, which has itself been taken private - a change worth watching for pipeline continuity.
9A4U.comp: Mapletree Logistics Trust, CapitaLand Ascendas REIT, AIMS APAC REIT.
9A4U.moat: Portfolio scale after the mergers and a sponsor development pipeline, though individual assets are commoditised.
9A4U.ind: Regional logistics demand is solid; Singapore industrial rents have been rising.
9A4U.risk: Sponsor instability after the ESR privatisation, plus refinancing at higher rates.
9A4U.implied: A high yield implies the market prices in execution and sponsor risk.
9A4U.debate: Bulls say a cheap, diversified industrial portfolio post-merger with rental upside. Bears note a messy merger history and uncertainty about the sponsor.
9A4U.disprove: Occupancy falling; gearing above 41%; distribution per unit declining; sponsor pipeline access unclear.

CY6U.what: Owns IT business parks, industrial facilities and data centres in Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad, Pune and Mumbai, and leases them to Indian and global IT firms.
CY6U.rev: Bangalore and Chennai business parks are the largest contributors. All income is in Indian rupees, distributed in Singapore dollars.
CY6U.gm: Net property income margins above 80%. It is a business trust, so it can develop assets directly rather than only buying completed ones.
CY6U.mgmt: Managed by CapitaLand Investment as sponsor - the first Indian property trust listed in Asia.
CY6U.comp: Embassy REIT, Mindspace REIT and DLF in Indian commercial property.
CY6U.moat: Established Indian business park portfolio with multinational tenants and a development pipeline - hard for a newcomer to assemble.
CY6U.ind: Indian office demand from global capability centres has been the strongest office market in the world.
CY6U.risk: Rupee depreciation eroding Singapore dollar distributions - the structural drag on this trust.
CY6U.implied: A high yield implies continued rupee weakness and development execution risk.
CY6U.debate: Bulls say the best-performing office market in the world at a high yield. Bears say currency depreciation has eaten much of the operating growth.
CY6U.disprove: Rupee depreciating faster than rental growth; occupancy falling; development projects delayed; gearing rising above 40%.

A50.what: Runs Thomson Medical Centre and womens and childrens clinics in Singapore, plus hospitals in Malaysia (TMC Life) and Vietnam (FV Hospital).
A50.rev: Singapore hospital and clinic services, Malaysian hospital operations and the Vietnamese FV Hospital acquired in 2023.
A50.gm: Hospital EBITDA margins in the teens to 20s. The Vietnam acquisition added debt and is the key integration question.
A50.mgmt: Controlled by Peter Lim, the Singapore investor. Governance and related-party matters are worth reading carefully.
A50.comp: Raffles Medical, IHH (Parkway) and Singapore Health Services in Singapore; local hospitals in Vietnam.
A50.moat: Brand in Singapore maternity care and hospital licences in three countries - real but narrow.
A50.ind: Regional private healthcare demand is growing, particularly in Vietnam.
A50.risk: Debt from the FV Hospital acquisition weighing on a business with modest earnings, plus Singapore birth rates falling.
A50.implied: The valuation implies successful Vietnam integration and earnings growth that has not yet appeared.
A50.debate: Bulls say regional private healthcare exposure with a well-known controlling shareholder. Bears point to leverage, thin profitability and declining Singapore births.
A50.disprove: Vietnam integration costs rising; net debt not falling; Singapore patient volumes declining; further equity fundraising.

F03.what: Makes and sells instant coffee mixes and snacks - MacCoffee and CafePHO - mainly in Russia, Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Vietnam and India.
F03.rev: Russia and Eastern Europe is the largest market, Southeast Asia (Vietnam) next and growing, with South Asia and ingredient manufacturing the rest.
F03.gm: Gross margin around 30-35%. Brand strength in specific markets supports pricing, but coffee bean costs have been extremely volatile.
F03.mgmt: Sudeep Nair is CEO; founder Tan Wang Cheow is executive chairman and the family controls the company. Dividends have been generous.
F03.comp: Nestle and local instant coffee brands in each market; Trung Nguyen in Vietnam.
F03.moat: Brand leadership in specific markets - MacCoffee is a household name in Russia and Kazakhstan - plus distribution reach.
F03.ind: Instant coffee consumption is growing in its emerging markets; Vietnam is the expansion focus.
F03.risk: Russia and Ukraine exposure - sanctions, currency and payment risk in the largest profit market.
F03.implied: A low-to-mid teens P/E implies continued growth with the Russia risk discounted.
F03.debate: Bulls say a genuinely growing consumer brand at a modest multiple with a strong dividend. Bears point at geopolitical concentration and coffee input cost inflation.
F03.disprove: Russian ruble depreciation or sanctions affecting cash repatriation; coffee bean costs compressing margins; Vietnam expansion stalling.

H13.what: Owns and develops property - Singapore residential (Sentosa Cove), and a large portfolio of UK and European commercial buildings.
H13.rev: Rental income from UK and Australian commercial properties provides the recurring base; Singapore residential development is lumpy.
H13.gm: Watch recurring rental income, net gearing and the discount to net asset value. UK office values have fallen significantly.
H13.mgmt: The Chua family controls it; Chua Thian Poh is chairman. Family control, conservative but concentrated in UK offices.
H13.comp: Other Singapore property companies with overseas portfolios - City Developments, Wing Tai, Frasers.
H13.moat: Asset ownership rather than competitive advantage. The UK portfolio is the key exposure.
H13.ind: UK commercial property values have fallen with higher rates; Singapore residential is constrained.
H13.risk: Further UK office valuation write-downs and refinancing at materially higher rates.
H13.implied: A very deep discount to net asset value implies the market expects more write-downs.
H13.debate: Bulls say assets at a fraction of book with a stable dividend. Bears note UK office exposure at exactly the wrong time and thin liquidity.
H13.disprove: UK portfolio revaluation losses; interest cover falling; net asset value per share declining; dividend cut.

P15.what: A holding company whose main asset is a large stake in PCCW, the Hong Kong telecom and media group.
P15.rev: Essentially the equity-accounted earnings and dividends from its PCCW shareholding, plus small management services.
P15.gm: Not meaningful - this is a single-asset holding company. Value it by the market value of its PCCW stake against the share price.
P15.mgmt: Richard Li controls it. Minority shareholders are passengers in a structure built around one controlling holder.
P15.comp: For an investor, buying PCCW directly in Hong Kong is the alternative.
P15.moat: None of its own - it inherits whatever advantages PCCW has in Hong Kong telecom.
P15.ind: Hong Kong telecom is mature; PCCW's data centre and insurance interests are the growth pieces.
P15.risk: The holding company discount persisting or widening, and dependence on PCCW dividend policy.
P15.implied: The price relative to the PCCW stake value tells you the discount the market applies.
P15.debate: Bulls say indirect PCCW exposure at a large discount. Bears say the discount has been permanent and liquidity is minimal.
P15.disprove: PCCW share price declining; PCCW cutting dividends; the discount widening; no buybacks or restructuring.

OU8.what: Builds, owns and operates purpose-built worker dormitories and student accommodation in Singapore, Malaysia, the UK, Australia and Hong Kong.
OU8.rev: Worker accommodation (Singapore and Malaysia) is the profit core; student accommodation in the UK and Australia the growth arm. It now also manages the spun-off Centurion Accommodation REIT.
OU8.gm: Very high operating margins on dormitories (above 60% EBITDA) given regulated bed supply and near-full occupancy.
OU8.mgmt: Kong Chee Min is CEO; the Loh and Han families control the company. The REIT spin-off in 2025 unlocked value and created a fee stream.
OU8.comp: Other Singapore dormitory operators and international student housing providers.
OU8.moat: Singapore dormitory licensing restricts supply, and existing operators with approved beds hold a regulated advantage.
OU8.ind: Migrant worker bed demand tracks construction and marine activity; student housing demand is structural.
OU8.risk: Government policy changes on dormitory standards or foreign worker quotas.
OU8.implied: After the REIT spin-off the price implies continued high occupancy plus growing management fees.
OU8.debate: Bulls say regulated supply, high occupancy and a new asset-light fee business. Bears note policy dependence and concentration in Singapore.
OU8.disprove: Occupancy falling; bed rates declining; foreign worker levies or quotas tightening; student accommodation expansion underperforming.

NC2.what: Produces and sells natural rubber - concentrated latex, block rubber and ribbed smoked sheet - mainly from Thailand.
NC2.rev: Natural rubber products sold to tyre manufacturers and glove makers worldwide. A Thai-primary company with an SGX secondary listing.
NC2.gm: Gross margin is thin and tracks the spread between raw rubber purchase prices and product selling prices.
NC2.mgmt: Controlled by the Sincharoenkul family of Thailand.
NC2.comp: Other Thai and Indonesian rubber processors; Sri Trang Gloves is a listed subsidiary.
NC2.moat: Scale in rubber processing and farmer sourcing networks in Thailand - cost position in a commodity.
NC2.ind: Natural rubber prices have been volatile; glove demand normalised after the pandemic surge.
NC2.risk: Rubber price swings and Thai baht strength compressing already thin margins.
NC2.implied: A low valuation implies the market expects thin, volatile margins to continue.
NC2.debate: Bulls say leverage to any rubber price upcycle. Bears note commodity processing with no pricing power and secondary-listing illiquidity.
NC2.disprove: Rubber prices falling; processing margins compressing; glove subsidiary losses; inventory write-downs.

P40U.what: Owns Wisma Atria and Ngee Ann City on Orchard Road plus retail and office assets in Australia, Malaysia, China and Japan.
P40U.rev: Singapore (Orchard Road) is roughly 60-65% of net property income, Australia ~25%, the rest smaller.
P40U.gm: REIT metrics: gearing around 36-37%, occupancy above 96%, with the Toshin master lease at Ngee Ann City a key income anchor.
P40U.mgmt: Managed by YTL Corporation of Malaysia as sponsor.
P40U.comp: CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust and Mapletree Pan Asia in Singapore retail.
P40U.moat: Orchard Road frontage - Singapore's premier shopping street - is genuinely scarce retail real estate.
P40U.ind: Orchard Road retail has recovered with tourism; Australian retail is stable.
P40U.risk: The Toshin master lease renewal terms, and Orchard Road losing relevance to suburban malls and online.
P40U.implied: A high yield and discount to book imply the market expects flat distributions.
P40U.debate: Bulls say prime Orchard Road assets at a discount with a high yield. Bears note years of flat distributions and limited growth.
P40U.disprove: Orchard Road tenant sales declining; Toshin lease renewed on worse terms; Australian occupancy falling; distribution cut.

G92.what: Supplies jet fuel to Chinese airports and trades oil products internationally, with a stake in the Shanghai Pudong airport refuelling joint venture.
G92.rev: Jet fuel supply and oil trading volumes are large, but the profit comes substantially from the equity-accounted Pudong refuelling joint venture.
G92.gm: Trading gross margins are razor thin - fractions of a percent. The associate income is the real earnings driver.
G92.mgmt: Controlled by China National Aviation Fuel Group, a Chinese state-owned enterprise.
G92.comp: Other jet fuel suppliers and oil traders; the Pudong joint venture is effectively a monopoly at that airport.
G92.moat: The Pudong airport refuelling concession is a genuine monopoly; the trading business has no moat at all.
G92.ind: Chinese international air traffic is still recovering from the pandemic, which drives refuelling volumes.
G92.risk: Chinese international flight volumes stalling, or the parent restructuring the relationship with minority shareholders.
G92.implied: A low P/E with a large net cash position implies little growth is expected.
G92.debate: Bulls say net cash exceeds a large share of the market cap with recovering Chinese aviation. Bears note state control, thin trading margins and minority shareholder risk.
G92.disprove: Pudong joint venture profits declining; Chinese international flights not recovering; trading losses; cash not returned.

AP4.what: Makes cleanroom gloves for semiconductor and electronics manufacturers, and healthcare gloves, from plants in Malaysia and Thailand.
AP4.rev: Cleanroom gloves are the higher-margin core; healthcare gloves are a more commoditised, competitive segment. Customers are global semiconductor and medical firms.
AP4.gm: Gross margin in the 20s-30s, much better in cleanroom than healthcare. Nitrile raw material costs and the ringgit drive swings.
AP4.mgmt: Wong Teek Son founded and runs the company with a substantial family stake. Net cash and consistent dividends.
AP4.comp: Top Glove, Hartalega and Kossan in Malaysia; Chinese producers competing aggressively on healthcare gloves.
AP4.moat: Cleanroom customer qualification is a genuine barrier - semiconductor fabs audit and approve suppliers over years.
AP4.ind: Semiconductor cleanroom demand tracks fab utilisation; healthcare gloves are oversupplied.
AP4.risk: Chinese glove makers dumping capacity into the healthcare segment and US tariff policy shifting demand.
AP4.implied: A low-to-mid teens P/E with a large net cash balance implies modest growth and continued dividends.
AP4.debate: Bulls like net cash, high dividend and a defensible cleanroom niche. Bears note glove overcapacity and customer concentration in semiconductors.
AP4.disprove: Cleanroom volumes declining; healthcare glove prices falling further; net cash being eroded; margin compression.

P52.what: Supplies ready-mix concrete and cement to Singapore construction projects - the largest concrete supplier in the country.
P52.rev: Concrete and cement is essentially the whole business after exiting shipping and ports. Singapore is the dominant market.
P52.gm: Gross margin in the low teens. Volume and mix (specialised low-carbon concrete carries better margins) drive profitability.
P52.mgmt: Ng Bok Eng and family control the company. Conservative balance sheet with net cash and rising dividends.
P52.comp: Other Singapore ready-mix suppliers and cement importers; Hong Leong Asia in building materials.
P52.moat: Batching plant locations near Singapore construction sites, long-term customer relationships and technical concrete formulations.
P52.ind: Singapore construction demand is strong - Changi Terminal 5, HDB building programme, industrial and data centre projects.
P52.risk: A construction slowdown after the current infrastructure pipeline, or cement import cost spikes.
P52.implied: A mid-teens P/E implies the Singapore construction pipeline keeps delivering volume growth.
P52.debate: Bulls say a direct, debt-free play on a visible multi-year Singapore construction pipeline. Bears note it is a cyclical commodity supplier with a small market.
P52.disprove: Singapore construction demand forecasts falling; concrete volumes declining; cement costs rising; margins compressing.

O5RU.what: Owns industrial, logistics and business park properties in Singapore and Australia and leases them to manufacturers and logistics firms.
O5RU.rev: Singapore is roughly 75-80% of net property income, Australia the rest. A diversified industrial portfolio with a large single-tenant exposure.
O5RU.gm: REIT metrics: net property income margin around 73%, gearing in the low-to-mid 30s (conservative for an S-REIT), occupancy in the mid 90s.
O5RU.mgmt: Managed by AIMS Financial Group. Smaller scale than the Mapletree or CapitaLand REITs, so acquisition capacity is limited.
O5RU.comp: ESR-REIT, Mapletree Industrial and Logistics Trusts, Sabana.
O5RU.moat: Portfolio of Singapore industrial assets - commoditised, but the low gearing gives more flexibility than peers.
O5RU.ind: Singapore industrial rents have been rising for several years on limited supply.
O5RU.risk: Tenant concentration - the loss of a large single tenant would hit distributions directly.
O5RU.implied: A yield above 7% implies the market expects limited growth and some tenant risk.
O5RU.debate: Bulls like low gearing, a high yield and positive Singapore industrial reversions. Bears note small scale, tenant concentration and limited growth capacity.
O5RU.disprove: A major tenant not renewing; occupancy falling below 93%; gearing rising; distribution per unit declining.

W05.what: Develops and invests in property in Singapore, Malaysia and Australia, and holds retail brand franchises in Singapore (Uniqlo joint venture).
W05.rev: Property development and investment plus a retail segment. The Uniqlo Singapore and Malaysia joint venture is a valuable but partly hidden asset.
W05.gm: Look at net asset value per share, net gearing (low), and the discount the shares trade at.
W05.mgmt: The Cheng family controls it; Cheng Wai Keung is chairman. Very conservative with a large net cash position.
W05.comp: UOL, City Developments, GuocoLand in Singapore property.
W05.moat: Asset ownership plus the Uniqlo franchise rights - the retail joint venture is the more interesting asset.
W05.ind: Singapore residential is constrained; retail franchise sales have been solid.
W05.risk: The discount to book never closing and development activity remaining minimal.
W05.implied: Trading at a very large discount to net asset value implies the market assigns little value to the assets or to future activity.
W05.debate: Bulls say a net-cash property company with a valuable Uniqlo stake at a third of book. Bears say it has been cheap for a decade with no catalyst.
W05.disprove: Net asset value per share declining; development pipeline empty; Uniqlo joint venture profit falling; no capital return.

S61.what: Operates public buses and the North East and Downtown MRT lines in Singapore under government contracts.
S61.rev: Public transport services (bus and rail fare and contract revenue) plus advertising and rental at stations. Singapore only.
S61.gm: Operating margins are thin and regulated. Bus operations run on a fixed-fee contracting model; rail carries more revenue risk.
S61.mgmt: A subsidiary of ComfortDelGro, which holds a controlling stake - free float is small.
S61.comp: SMRT operates the other rail lines; bus packages are competitively tendered by the Land Transport Authority.
S61.moat: Operating concessions granted by the government - secure while they last, but repriced at renewal.
S61.ind: Ridership has recovered above pre-pandemic levels; fare adjustments follow a regulated formula.
S61.risk: Rail operating costs rising faster than the fare formula allows, or losing bus packages at tender.
S61.implied: A low-teens P/E with a high dividend implies stable contract earnings with no growth.
S61.debate: Bulls say a regulated, cash-generative operator with a high payout. Bears note capped returns, parent control and minimal free float.
S61.disprove: Rail operating losses returning; bus packages lost at tender; fare formula adjustments unfavourable; dividend cut.

B61.what: Develops and sells landed and high-end residential property in Singapore, from a historic land bank in the Sembawang and Seletar areas.
B61.rev: Residential development sales, which are lumpy and project-dependent, plus a small investment property and hospitality segment.
B61.gm: Development margins depend on land cost basis - the legacy land bank was acquired decades ago at very low cost, which flatters margins.
B61.mgmt: Controlled by the Lee family (also behind OCBC). Conservative, net cash, and content to develop slowly.
B61.comp: Other Singapore residential developers - UOL, GuocoLand, City Developments.
B61.moat: A low-cost historic land bank that cannot be replicated at today's land prices.
B61.ind: Singapore landed housing is a restricted market open mainly to citizens - limited supply, resilient prices.
B61.risk: Cooling measures slowing sales, and earnings that appear only when projects complete.
B61.implied: Trading below book implies the market discounts the slow pace of development.
B61.debate: Bulls say cheap legacy land, net cash and special dividends when projects complete. Bears note lumpy earnings, thin liquidity and a passive controlling family.
B61.disprove: Project launches delayed; landed property prices falling; net asset value per share declining; dividends stopping.

E28.what: Provides contract design and manufacturing for semiconductor equipment, medical, analytical and industrial automation customers in Europe and Asia.
E28.rev: Semiconductor is the largest segment (ASML is a key customer), with medical, analytical and industrial automation the rest. Netherlands, Singapore, Malaysia and China operations.
E28.gm: Gross margin around 14-16% - lower than Venture because more of the work is assembly than design.
E28.mgmt: Gooi Soon Chai is CEO. The founding families retain stakes. Conservative balance sheet.
E28.comp: Venture Corporation, VDL and other European contract manufacturers, plus Asian peers.
E28.moat: Qualified supplier status with demanding customers like ASML, where changing manufacturer requires re-qualification.
E28.ind: Semiconductor equipment demand is recovering; medical and analytical markets have been soft.
E28.risk: Customer concentration in semiconductor equipment, and thin margins that leave little room for error.
E28.implied: A mid-teens P/E implies a semiconductor recovery lifting volumes and margins.
E28.debate: Bulls say leverage to the ASML supply chain at a modest multiple. Bears note thin margins, customer concentration and cyclicality.
E28.disprove: Semiconductor segment revenue declining; gross margin below 14%; medical and analytical weakness persisting; capacity underutilised.
